extracted.intended_audience: health insurance issuers, State regulators, and public stakeholders/commenters
extracted.subtask_description: Extracted rubric covers proposed regulatory changes to essential health benefits (EHB) typicality, actuarial value (AV) methodology, multi-year catastrophic plan design (including cost-sharing and disclosures), and new cost-sharing parameters for bronze and catastrophic plans under the Affordable Care Act. It is aimed at commenters and regulated entities evaluating and implementing the proposed rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typicality test actuarial value calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: States must ensure the value of covering all the benefits in the State's proposed EHB-benchmark plan is between (or equal to) the value of the least and most generous typical employer plans in the State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nothing in regulation prohibits a State from including the quantitative value of routine non-pediatric dental services, routine non-pediatric eye exam services, long-term/custodial nursing home care benefits, or non-medically necessary orthodontia in its typicality analysis if a typical employer plan used in the typicality comparison includes any of these services; those services' actuarial value may be included when calculating that employer plan's overall value for purposes of the typicality test. However, allowing inclusion in the typicality calculation does not mean those services may be covered as EHBs in the State's EHB-benchmark plan itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on including routine non-pediatric dental as an EHB (proposed §156.115(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal to revise §156.115(d) to prohibit issuers from including routine non-pediatric dental services as an EHB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS seeks comment on the proposal including the impact on health insurance coverage in the individual, small group, and large group markets, and on self-insured plans. If finalized as proposed, the prohibition would be effective upon the effective date of the final rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of PAPI, MOOP, reduced MOOP, and required contribution percentage in guidance (§156.130(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: For benefit years in which HHS is not changing the methodology, HHS will publish the premium adjustment percentage index (PAPI), the required contribution percentage, maximum annual limitation on cost sharing (MOOP), and reduced MOOP in guidance annually by January of the year preceding the benefit year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 2025 Marketplace Integrity and Affordability final rule changed the methodology to use private health coverage premiums (excluding Medigap and the medical portion of accident/property and casualty insurance) for calculating the premium adjustment percentage and related parameters. HHS is not proposing further methodological changes for the 2027 benefit year and published the 2027 parameters in guidance using the methodology finalized in 2025.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible plan terms for catastrophic plans (§156.155)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal to specify that a catastrophic plan has a plan term of either 1 plan or policy year, or of multiple consecutive plan or policy years not to exceed 10 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issuers could choose multi-year terms up to a maximum of 10 years and could offer multiple multi-year plans with different maximum terms. Issuers would not be required to offer a 1-year plan identical to each multi-year plan. All other applicable Federal requirements and guaranteed availability/renewability rules would continue to apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value-based insurance design for multi-year catastrophic plans (section 2713(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Catastrophic plans with terms of at least 2 plan or policy years may utilize value-based insurance designs to offer benefits for preventive services without the enrollee having to first satisfy their deductible or annual cost-sharing limitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This clarification is provided under authority at section 2713(c) of the PHS Act. HHS seeks comment on the types of benefits plans could offer under this proposal (e.g., benefits designed to improve long-term health). Any such benefits must satisfy all applicable non-discrimination requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Option to apply annual limitation on cost sharing annually or averaged over contract
rubrics_metrics.description: Issuers of multi-year catastrophic plans may apply the annual limitation on cost sharing for each plan year on an annual basis, or on average over the life of the contract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: A 5-year catastrophic plan could apply the annual limitation so that the average over 5 years equals the statutory average; or vary annual limitations by disease (e.g., cancer) provided the average over all participants and years equals the required average. HHS requests comment on the proposal and on using monthly limits derived by dividing the annual limitation by 12 to determine monthly limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan-level adjustment to index rate for multi-year catastrophic plans (§156.80(d)(2)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal to amend §156.80(d)(2)(ii) to allow issuers of multi-year catastrophic plans to make a plan-level adjustment to the index rate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This adjustment is intended to promote innovation in plan design that could lower premiums and costs, while increasing access to coverage and improving health outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility at time of enrollment for multi-year catastrophic plans
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual must satisfy the statutory requirements for a catastrophic plan at the time of enrollment in the multi-year plan under section 1302(e)(2) of the Affordable Care Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS seeks comments on this proposal and how it would interact with other laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consumer and issuer effects rationale for multi-year terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Multi-year plan terms may increase issuer incentives to invest in long-term health interventions and reduce administrative costs associated with marketing and enrollment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS describes expected benefits like better adherence to disease management, predictable monthly out-of-pocket limits, and potential to reflect administrative efficiencies in lower premiums. Comments are requested on whether multi-year terms would make plans more affordable and on specific durations that incentivize long-term, health-promoting behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monthly application of annual limitation on cost sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: Issuers choosing the monthly method would divide the annual limitation on cost sharing by 12 to determine a monthly limit on cost sharing under the plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS views this approach as consistent with how the annual limitation must be calculated by plans and indicates that monthly limits would provide consistent, predictable monthly out-of-pocket limits and reduce consumer confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of deductible across multi-year term
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the proposal, issuers could apply the deductible that applies in the first year of coverage on an annual basis for each year within the coverage, or divide the annual deductible by 12 and apply it equally to each month of the policy throughout the entire term of coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: A $6,000 annual deductible could be applied as $500 per month. HHS seeks comment on whether and to what degree a plan could modify the amount of the annual deductible for each year of the multi-year policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuous coverage and termination rules for multi-year plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Current policy allows enrollees to terminate enrollment in a multi-year catastrophic plan at any time without penalty; issuers could discontinue the product or exit the market under guaranteed renewability exceptions applicable under section 2703 of the PHS Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS seeks comment on Federal policy options to promote continuous coverage in multi-year plans and defray risk of termination by either party, including through use of Individual Coverage Health Reimbursement Arrangements (ICHRAs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure requirements for multi-year catastrophic plans
rubrics_metrics.description: All multi-year catastrophic plans would be expected to disclose that the plan has a multi-year term, and the length of that term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a plan uses the monthly method of applying the annual limitation on cost sharing, plans would be expected to include that information in marketing and enrollment materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continued applicability of federal laws and program rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Multi-year catastrophic plans would continue to be subject to guaranteed availability and guaranteed renewability requirements and other Federal laws (e.g., Mental Health Parity and Addiction Equity Act; The Women's Health and Cancer Rights Act; Newborns' and Mothers' Health Protection Act; Michelle's Law; No Surprises Act).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individuals dropping coverage mid-term or at term-end would be treated the same as under 1-year plans with respect to open enrollment and special enrollment periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of HHS risk adjustment and MLR treatment for multi-year plans
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS will consider how to treat multi-year catastrophic plans for purposes of the HHS-operated risk adjustment program and whether modifications to risk adjustment regulations (45 CFR part 153) or MLR rules (45 CFR part 158) are needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions for comment include whether to use the same catastrophic HHS risk adjustment models for multi-year plans, whether to calculate risk adjustment transfers separately for multi-year plans, whether to modify the State average premium term in the State payment transfer formula, and whether multi-year plans should be considered under the same book of business for MLR purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for comment on issuer incentives, barriers, and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS requests comment on what incentives or disincentives issuers would have to offer multi-year catastrophic plans, potential administrative barriers, and how long it would take issuers to develop and offer these plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS also asks whether to require or permit multi-year terms for individual market catastrophic and metal level plans, and if so, which ones and why.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interaction with market rules and rating practices
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS requests comment on potential interactions between multi-year plans and health insurance market rules in 45 CFR parts 144 and 147, including guaranteed availability/renewability, fair health insurance premiums, age rating limits (3:1), and uniform modifications to coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS asks whether more regulatory changes would be needed to implement multi-year plans and how premiums and rating practices might differ for multi-year plans compared to conventional 1-year catastrophic plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interaction with tax-advantaged accounts (HSAs) and ICHRA
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS requests comment on how multi-year catastrophic plan proposals would interact with tax policy such as health savings accounts (HSAs) and individual coverage health reimbursement arrangements (ICHRAs), and whether changes to those laws or this proposal are needed to resolve conflicts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters should identify conflicts and suggest changes either to the proposal or to other laws to resolve such conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal to change permissible cost-sharing parameters for bronze and catastrophic plans (§156.136 and §156.155(a)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: To mitigate an actuarial implementation issue that threatens issuer ability to design plans within statutory AV/de minimis constraints, HHS proposes new optional cost-sharing parameters for bronze plans (§156.136) and revisions to catastrophic cost-sharing requirements (§156.155(a)(3)) in the individual market only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is presented as necessary because discrepancies in the rates of change among the three AV components (standard population, MOOP, EHB costs) can make issuer compliance with statutory provisions mathematically impossible without adopting new cost-sharing parameters or revising existing rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actuarial Value (AV) calculation components
rubrics_metrics.description: AV is the anticipated covered medical spending for coverage of EHB paid by a health plan (1) for a standard population, (2) computed in accordance with the plan's cost sharing (capped by the maximum annual limitation on cost sharing), and (3) divided by the total anticipated allowed charges for EHB coverage provided to the standard population.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three major components: (1) The Standard Population (derived from EDGE data with adjustments/weighting); (2) The Maximum Annual Limitation on Cost Sharing (statutorily set and updated using PAPI); (3) EHB Costs (projected with a trend factor for medical and prescription drugs using URRTs and National Health Expenditure data). Year-over-year changes in each component influence AV changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard population maintenance for AV Calculator
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS develops and provides a standard population for the AV Calculator that resembles enrollees likely to be covered by individual and small group market health insurance in a particular year, derived from enrollee-level EDGE data with adjustments and weighting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annual updates to the standard population reflect generally accepted actuarial principles and methodologies; failure to update would make the AV Calculator increasingly nonrepresentative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum annual limitation on cost sharing (statutory PAPI linkage)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1302(c) sets the MOOP and requires HHS to update it annually; for years after 2014 the MOOP is the product of the 2014 value and the PAPI (percentage change in average per capita premium), and for other than self-only coverage the MOOP is twice the self-only limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS releases PAPI via §156.130(e) guidance in years without methodological changes. Changes in MOOP impact AV (higher MOOP decreases AV). Example: MOOP increased from $6,350 in 2014 to $12,000 in 2027 (self-only).

rubrics_metrics.name: EHB cost trend factor practice
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS projects historical claims data for medical items/services and prescription drugs covered as EHB for the standard population for the next plan year; this projection is the trend factor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trend factors have historically been set between specified ranges (medical: 3.25%-6.50%; drugs: 6.50%-11.50%). HHS reviews URRTs and National Health Expenditure data to select the health care cost update, which affects AV because higher costs increase plan generosity (i.e., raise AV).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to maintain AV integrity and limits on methodological tinkering
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS expresses that continued ad hoc modifications to the AV Calculator methodology or excessive expansion of de minimis ranges to preserve bronze plans would undermine the integrity of AV calculation and exceed statutory authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS highlights the tradeoff between preserving plan availability and maintaining fidelity to generally accepted actuarial principles; it identifies the long-term risk that MOOP may be too low to permit feasible AV calculations for basic bronze designs and therefore proposes targeted changes (optional bronze parameters and catastrophic revisions) instead of continuing methodological fixes.

rubrics_metrics.name: AV conformity to de minimis ranges (§156.140)
rubrics_metrics.description: Plans must generally conform to the de minimis AV variation ranges established under section 1302(d)(3) and codified at §156.140; issuers have narrowed options for cost-sharing adjustments when AV trends change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS notes that expansions to de minimis ranges (e.g., expanded bronze) have been used before to allow plan viability but cautions against further adjustments that would approach statutory limits. HHS describes how rising AV causes bronze plans to appear more like silver plans, undermining tier distinctions.
